data.description: The site of Agham Kot is located about 33.88 km north-east of Matli city and about 1.88 km north of Ghulab Khan Leghari. It can be accessed from Ghulab Laghari via link road. The historic city of Agham Kot also locally known as Aghamano has been mentioned in old historic documents Chach Nama and Tohfat-ul-Karam, as a town which was situated on the bank of old course of river Indus and flourished for years, it was the capital town of Buddhist ruler Raja Agham Luhano who ruled the area before the Arabs invaded Sindh. The city was destroyed by an Afghan invader Madad Khan Pathan who ransacked the whole city at the end of 18th century, whereas some scholars relate its decline on the change in the river course which once flowed beside it. Agham Kot is a large settlement site with profusion of cultural material scattered in various parts of the site. Presently it is in a ruinous condition. It is encroached by agricultural activities surrounding the site, resulting in the loss of evidence of earlier period.

data.description: Pir Hamid Shah Mosque also known as Wahanee mosque, is located in Pir Hamid Shah Graveyard, it is in a ruined condition and once it was very elegant structure beautifully built. It originally had three-domes and now only central dome is surviving. Three-domed mosques were mostly constructed in Kalhora period. The facade of the mosque is on the eastern side, the original dimensions of the mosque were 16.8 x 6.8 m and the total covered area was 115.66 sq.m. The mosque was constructed with burnt bricks (22.8 x 22.8 x 3.8 cm), mud was used as mortar and cheroli was used in 1st layer of the plaster, lime and jute in 2nd layer and 3rd finishing layer with lime cream and soap stone. The facade of the mosque was originally decorated with three multifoil arch openings within recessed multifoil arches, presently only two openings are surviving in a ruined condition. Two domes have collapsed whereas the central dome which is surviving, rests on an octagonal drum and the perimeter of the drum is decorated with merlons and there are two ventilators and four protruding squinches on the external side of the drum. In the interior of the mosque, the central drum is decorated with four squinches alternating with recessed Tudor arch panels and muqarnas, with two panels having ventilators. There are some traces of secco painting visible in the interior of the mosque.

data.description: Located on Makli hills on south of the Archaeological campus at a distance of about 8 km are the extensive remains of a ruined fort once known as Kalan Kot or Tughluabad. This fort, according to Tarikh-i-Masumi, is said to have been constructed by Mirza Jani Beg somewhere in the last quarter of 16th Century CE on the site of an earlier fort built by Jam Taghur or Tughluk on the site of a still earlier Hindu fort. Mirza Jani Beg, while fighting with emperor Akbar`s troops under Khan Khanan, wrote to his father Payndah Beg and his son Abul Fateh who were at Thatta, to construct a Fort as a place of refuge, should he be compelled to flee before the enemy. He further desired, under such circumstances, the city of Thatta should be abandoned to its fate and they should take themselves a long with the peoples to Kalankot. So was done, we are told, and the city of Thatta was laid waste for short duration. The fort is extensive and appears to be an irregular oblong in plan. The fort wall which has considerable thickness and together with its circular bastions is built with a core of mud, bricks lined on either side with a layer of burnt bricks laid in mud mortar. The thickness of this burnt brick, lining course is about 10 inches. From the structural remains which are still available on the site. It is quite evident that the entire area of the fort was divided into different sectors each beset with various type of residential buildings. Nothing is left of such a big fort except some dilapidated portion of the fortification wall or ruined bastions. The only conspicuous features among the remains are the ruined mosque with a big tank in front of it. The rough extent of the mosque may be taken as 76.2 x 50.2 m and that of the tank 29.2 x 26.5 x 4.2 m. What remains now of the mosque is the main roofless prayer chamber with its main entrance arch on east the thickness of which is 3 m. The existing height of the walls is about 7.5 m. In the mehrab on west there are remains of honey-combed plaster work. The Jambs and spandrels of the upper niches are lined with white/blue glazed tiles the traces of which can still be seen. The floor of the mosque was paved with plain tiles. The main entrance arch of the mosque has been lined with cut and dressed brick tiles laid in mud mortar but the visible joints deeply treated with lime cheroli mortar. A damaged stone pulpit beautifully carved in floral design also occupies the space in NW corner of the mosque. The tank lying in front of the mosque is deeply out in rock lined with bricks laid in lime mortar and finally covered with thick lime plaster.

data.description: The graveyard of Dau-Ja-Quba is located about 32km north-west of Ghaibi dero village. It can be accessed from Ghaibi Dero to Sono Khan Chandio village and off via earthen track to the graveyard. The graveyard is known as Dau-ja-Quba, it is named after Dau who was the chief of the Hussaini tribe and was killed in 1614 in the battle of Mahu near Ghaibi Dero. The graveyard consists of eight tombs beautifully decorated with fresco and some old and recent graves in the surroundings. The graveyard belongs to Kalhora period. The tomb I belongs to Dau Khan Chandio, it is square in shape and is constructed with burnt bricks with mud mortar and traditional lime plaster. The facade of the tomb is on the eastern side, it has a high recessed rectangular frame in the center with a large and small Tudor arch for the entrance. On both sides of the central panel there are four recessed rectangular panels with two horizontal panels above them. The parapet of the facade is decorated with merlons and turrets. In the interior of the tomb, there are deep squinches going down to the floor level alternating with large Tudor arches in the center, within these arches, there is Mehrab in the western wall, entrance in the eastern, whereas the southern and northern side arch panel has an arch and panels.

data.description: Gaji Shah site is located approximately 1.5 km east of Pir Ghazi Shah Mausoleum and village. It can be accessed from Johi via Chinni road towards Ghazi Shah. The mound of Gaji Shah also known as Mari Khar, measures 162 m north-south and 132 m east-west and the total area of the occupation on the mound is 21384 sq.m, it is about 6.7 m high from the surrounding plains. The site was discovered by N.G Majumdar in the early 30`s (1930-1931), it was later visited and intermittently excavated by Dr. Louis Flam from 1975 onwards. The Sindh archaeological project of Dr. Flam was initiated in 1985-1987, 1997-98 and 2001. Majumdar had named the site Gaji Shah, because of its being near the mausoleum of a well-known saint Pir Gaji Shah in the east, at a distance of about 1.5 km. The artifactual evidence uncovered by Majumdar and Dr. Flam in their excavations and in the recent survey in March 2017 by CDC team, clearly portray it to be Early and Mature Indus site with the presence of Amrian, Mature Indus, Kulli, Nal and Mehi cultural evidence.

data.description: Kotero Daro is located approximately 2.65 km north of Wahi Pandhi town, it can be accessed from Wahi Pandhi via earthen track towards Kotero Daro. Kotero site also known as Wahi Pandh is occupied with Muslim period graves with Amrian and Mature Indus pottery (3500-1850 B.C) scattered on the surface. It was first discovered by N.G Majumdar, during his exploration of Sindh Kohistan. The mound as recorded by Dr. Louis Flam was 6 m high and the total area of the mound was 12,733 sq.m, but presently the mound is 6 m high from the surrounding plains and the total occupied area is about 9000 sq.m, nearly 2900 sq.m area is destroyed due to agricultural activity around the mound (survey of March 2017). The site has suffered considerable ravages at the hands of local people. The mound is situated north of Wahi Pandhi. It stands near Raj Wah (branch of hill torrent Nai Narri or Nalli). This mound is also locally called as Kotero Daro, but N.G Majumdar had named it Wahi Pandhi. He excavated two trenches and two pits at Wahi Pandhi and claimed the site to be of Neolithic and chalcolithic period. He wrote that the great antiquity of the site is proved by the black and red Indus pottery, cherty flakes, terracotta bangles, stone lying scattered over the site. In the recent survey in March 2017 by CDC team, it clearly portrays it to be Early and Mature Indus site with the presence of Amrian and Mature Indus cultural material. The cultural material found on surface during the survey included: terracotta cakes, bangles, toy cart wheels, balls, lid and horn. Painted and plain pottery of typical Mature Indus and Amrian period, including perforated jars and some small pieces of copper.

data.description: Matan Shah graveyard is located in Shah Hassan Village on the western bank of Manchar Lake, about 39 km south of Johi town. It can be accessed from Johi via Shah Hassan link road towards Matan Shah graveyard. Matan Shah graveyard consists of two tomb structures (Tomb 01 of Matan Shah and Tomb 02 (Unknown) and some old and recent graves in the surroundings. The date mentioned on the tomb of Matan Shah is 1284 A.H. On the basis of architectural resemblance, the tomb structures are placed within the chronological bracket of the Talpur period.

data.description: The tomb of Muhammad Khan Bhutto is located about 16.8 km north of Shahdadkot city in Daro Mengal Murad village. The site lies west off Shahdadkot-Garhi Khairo road and further via earthen track of about 4.70 km to the village Daro Mengal Murad. Muhammad Khan Bhutto tomb is situated within a graveyard which comprises of a tomb, one Dargah (renovated) and recent graves in the surroundings. It is square in plan and constructed with two sizes of burnt bricks with mud mortar and lime plaster.The facade of the tomb is on the eastern side, with a recessed rectangular panel having a large multifoil arch and a smaller arched entrance in the center. On either side of the main arch, is a recessed rectangular and Tudor arch panel. There is a cornice around the tomb and closed kiosks on each corner. The dome rests on an octagonal drum. The drum is decorated with recessed rectangular frames with multifoil decoration.

data.description: Bhando Qubo site is located about 3.32 Km east of Rato Dero town, it can be accessed from Rato Dero town via N-55 road to Dakhan, Taluka Rato Dero, District Larkana. There is a tomb situated on top of the mound belonging to Rato Khan Jalbani, the legendary founder of Ratodero who died defending his land from bands of invaders in the 18th century CE The mound on which the tomb is situated is of Early and Mature Indus period deduced from the section clearing and small-scale excavation carried out by Department of Archaeology Shah Abdul Latif University Khairpur (SALU) in 1997, under the direction of Dr. Nilofer Shaikh.

data.description: Tharo Kot is located about 1 km north-east of Shah Deewano village. It can be accessed from Matli-Tando Ghulam Ali road via link road towards Shah Deewano village.Tharo Kot is in a ruined condition and only some traces of a fortification wall of burnt bricks with mud mortar are surviving. These walls are visible on two sides, western (167.64 m) and northern (233 m), whereas on the southern side traces are visible for about 40 m on the surface. There is evidence of a room like structure and a robber`s trench on the northern wall.

data.description: The Mazar Bhurgri Thul is located approximately 4.26 km north-east of Qasbo village. It can be accessed from Pat Gul Muhammad-Qasbo Road towards village Mazar Bhurgri.The Thul/ Stupa Mazar Bhurgri is of the Buddhist period, the remains of such Thul/ stupas of Buddhist period are found in various parts of Sindh. These stupas or Thul were most probably constructed between 3rd-7th century CE in Sindh. The Thul is irregular in shape and about 4 m high from the surface level. The measurement of the base on the eastern side is 10 m, western 7.3 m, southern 10 m and northern 9.5 m. It is partially eroded with the passage of the time. It is constructed with mud bricks, there are some molded bricks scattered surrounding the Thul, perhaps, they were used in the base for decoration. Burnt bricks, molded /decorated bricks and brick bats along with stamped pottery are scattered on the surface near the Thul. There are traces of burnt brick wall at a distance about 30 m, on the western side of the Thul.

data.description: Ahedi Faqir graveyard is located in village Peeral Khan Shahani about 22 km south-west of Johi town and about 04 km south of village Chinni. It can be accessed from Johi via village Chinni link road towards Ahedi Faqeer Graveyard. The tomb of Ahedi Faqir is located at a distance of about 2.5 km south of village Chinni in the Chinni hills. The site is occupied with ancient graves. Local version is that Ahedi Faqir was a Panhwar by caste, no historic records are traceable, however, the tomb architecture resembles with Kalhora period architecture. The tomb is square in shape and constructed with burnt bricks. Cheroli has been used as mortar with lime plaster. An entrance to the tomb has been provided through tudor arch with modern iron door (later addition) to the southern side. The facade is flanked by two vertical arched panels, whereas three sides of the tomb are decorated with two horizontal arched panels and one rectangular panel, presently the painting on the exterior walls has faded. The dome rests on the low octagonal drum. The dome is crowned on top with inverted lotus and remains of a rod of the finial. There are four kiosks one in each corner. Few merlons have survived on the parapet wall and on the octagonal drum. Inside the tomb there are two graves laid down in single row repaired with cement. Mehrab is on the west which is painted with beautiful fresco designs as well as Quranic verses. The interior of the tomb is ornamented with beautiful naturalistic (floral and faunal) and geometrical motifs in fresco and there are some interesting murals depicting fruit images. Repair work has been done with cement on the floor.

data.description: The Canopy of Shahdad Faqir Langha lies about 80 m south of Mian Yar Muhammad Kalhoro mausoleum and about 3 km west of Khudabad mosque Dadu.The canopy of Shahdad Faqir Langha is located near the Mausoleum of Mian Yar Muhammad Kalhoro. According to local version the canopy belongs to Shahdad Faqir Langha, but no historic records are available regarding Shadad Faqir Langha. The canopy of Shahdad Faqir Langha is built with yellow color stone; it is erected over a double stepped platform, there is a yellow carved stone border surviving on one side of the first platform with beautiful motifs/designs in the shape of rosette and other floral and geometrical designs. The other three sides of the border have been repaired and plastered with cement. The canopy is square in plan and is erected on the second platform with the support of eight pillars. All the Pillars of the canopy are divided into three parts (base, shaft and capital) carved with geometric, floral and sun flower designs. The dome rests on the octagonal drum. Presently the dome has collapsed. The parapet is crowned by a series of pointed arched shaped merlons having various decorative motifs around the canopy and there is only one grave inside the canopy.

data.description: The graveyard of Mureed Jamali is located at a distance of about 5 km to the west of Hairo Khan village and about 1 km south of village Mureed Dero, it can be accessed via Hairo Khan earthen track towards Mureed Dero. The graveyard consists of four structures (one tomb and three canopies) one of the canopies belongs to Mureed Jamali and some old and recent graves are scattered around these structures. Mureed Jamali was known to be the commander of the Mianwal Movement during the reign of Mian Naseer Muhammad Kalhoro (1657-1692CE). He lived in the village Mureed Dero and was buried in Mureed Jamali graveyard, since then the graveyard is known as Mureed Jamali graveyard (Kalhora Period).

data.description: The tomb of Veeral Shah is located about 02 km north-west of Borarri village and can be accessed from Khairpur Nathan Shah-Borarri village road. The structure perhaps was a Darbar of Guru Gorakhnath and was in the possession of the Hindu community at the time of partition. There was a perhaps a Samadhi inside this Darbar, presently it known as Veeral Shah tomb by the locals. Surrounding this structure, there are some old structures including one well, mud bricks wall, water pool and a pipal tree.The Veeral Shah tomb (Veernath temple) was originally enclosed within a earthen wall with an entrance of burnt bricks, traces of which are still surviving. Presently the structure is concealed by trees and wild growth. The structure is almost square in shape; the facade of the structure is on the eastern side. It has high recessed rectangular panel with lancet Gothic arch entrance within a larger recessed tudor arch. The dome rests on the structure and there is no drum. The dome is surmounted by inverted lotus moulding and a finial. The interior of the structure has tudor arch shaped squinches on the four sides and an open niche shaped ventilator on the western wall. There is one grave laid on a rectangular platform which is enclosed within burnt brick wall. In the Interior few traces of fresco painting are visible above the squinches and dome.

Internally each wall has a deep recessed arched panel. The tomb is associated to Talpur period of Historic Sindh (1783-1847 CE).

data.description: It is also known as Kot Raja Manjera. The site was described as the ruins of a Buddhist site and a stupa. Cousen also identified the site with the remains of a Buddhist Stupa. Professor A.R. Khan of Karachi University who surveyed it in the early 1970s (KHAN, 1979a: 6) identified the top of the terrace as prehistoric site and attributed it to the Amri Culture due to the presence of typical red-slipped wares and potshards with painted geometric patterns (KHAN, 1979b: 71), and a rich chipped stone assemblage, including flint micro drills for beads making. According to the field notes by A.R. KHAN (1979a: 7) the site yielded archaeological finds, which he attributed to both Amri Culture and Buddhist period (5th century CE).
data.title: Inventory of Cultural Property in the Province of Sindh, Pakistan, 2015

data.description: In the midst of the ruins of the old town of Khudabad stands the great massive Kalhora period (18th Century CE) Jamia Masjid. It is lavishly decorated with enameled tiles. The entrance of the mosque is lavishly decorated with panels of local Sindhi tiles on either side. It was built of Mian Yar Muhammad Kalhoro during his reign (1701-1718 CE). The floral patterns are disposed more or less in geometrical forms. It represents a tall and graceful plant lily order whose leaves, flowers and buds sprout from the central stem and fall over right and left in easy natural curves. The prayer chamber is divided into two equal compartments. The eastern compartment, a roofless one is a small hall. The hall seems to have a low flat roof, providing an access to the gallery achieved at the squinch level of the western domed compartment. Massive piers supporting the elegant arches divide the western hall into three aisles, the central one larger in side than the flanking one. Each bay has an arched mihrab sunk in the western wall.

data.description: In the last quarter of the 18th century Mir Fateh Ali Khan Talpur shifted his capital from Khudabad to Hyderabad and divided his kingdom into seven states. Major part of Khairpur division fell to the share of Mir Suhrab Khan the great grandfather of Mirs of Khairpur. He established his headquarter at Kot Diji and built this fort. It is situated on a high mound to the west of Kot Diji town, a strategic position of the hillock of which three sides are scraped almost perpendicular, while on the east side the ascent is extremely steep guarded by strong defenses. The fort can be approached through three strong gateways in the east on different terraces. A pavilion built in beautiful cut stone work command the east defenses and was probably the seat of Nawab. The semi-circular bastions were commanded with heavy guns of which only a brass gun known as Mariam remains there.

data.description: Bambhore is situated on the northern bank of the Gharo Creek. Excavations here exposed the earliest Muslim settlement of the subcontinent. The remains of a fortified city with cultural material of three distinct periods i.e., Scytho-Parthian, Hindu-Buddhist and the Islamic datable from the 1st century BCE to the 13th century CE were exposed. The fortified citadel of Bambhore is enclosed by a massive fortification wall having semi-circular bastions at regular intervals, three gateways, one each in the east, north-east and south respectively, an anchorage near the southern gate, an industrial area outside the citadel and the grand mosque which is considered to be the earliest mosque in the sub-continent besides residential houses with streets, lanes and by-lanes cutting one another at right angles.

data.description: It is located inside the Makli Hill necropolis near the tomb of Jam Nizamuddin. Tomb of Jam Mubarak Khan was constructed in 895 Hijrah, 1490 CE during the reign of Jam Nizamuddin II alias Jam Nando ruler of Samma dynasty. Jam Mubarak Khan also known as Dulha Darya Khan was the adopted son of Jam Nizamudin Nando and his Commander-in-Chief. Jam Mubarak was given the title of Khan-e-Azam and was martyred by Mughals (Mangols) in 895 Hijrah, 1490 CE.  The tomb of Jam Mubarak Khan situated in a quadrangle of high walls is built with carved stone blocks and jeweled with inscribed Arabic inscriptions by the Mason. It stands in close proximity to the mehrab, cut into the western wall of the enclosure. The enclosure walls are pierced by two door-openings one of the south and the other on the east wall. An Arabic inscription inscribed on the tomb of Mubarak Khan identifies the eternal abode of Mubarak Khan, while  the lintel of the eastern door also contains an Arabic inscription which gives the date of construction of this complex in the year eight hundred and ninety five 895 A.H. (April, 1409 CE)”. The Headstone on the graves of Mubarak Khan is topped by a turban in the shape of a lotus. An Arabic inscription inscribed on the tomb of Mubarak Khan reads: (Translation) “This resting place is for the exalted Khan Mubarak Khan the martyr son of Sultan Nizamuddin”. Similarly, the lintel of the eastern door is inscribed with an Arabic inscription which reads: (Translation) “The edifice (is built) in the time of the great Khan, Mian Mubarak Khan son of Sultan Nizamddin Shah the benevolent and the beloved of Allah; the construction (began) in the month of Jumadi-I in the year eight hundred and ninety five 895 A.H. (April, 1409 CE)”.
data.title: Inventory of Cultural Property in the Province of Sindh, Pakistan, 2015

data.name_of_site: Tomb of Jan Baba at Makli Hills
data.description:
It is located inside the Makli Hills necropolis of Thatta, to the east of Mirza Isa Khan Tarkhan-II on the southern fringe of the Makli hills The tomb of Jan Baba is constructed amazingly with excellent piece of architecture designed on the walls of the tomb. The stone are carved and joint beautifully which enhances its beauty and attracts visitors. Tomb is decorated with floral designs & geometric Medallions. The bricks from which the tomb building are of very high quality and perfectly baked. Enamel tiles which were used in the construction reflect Persian designs while the stone carving and other such elements reflects indigenous styles mixed with. Pakistan is the city with beautiful sceneries and also for the historical building which attracts many people towards it. People should visit these tombs and see the great art works which were done by earlier people. Built in 1664 CE by his son Isa Khan Tarkhan-II. Jan Baba was killed in rivalry with his brother Mirza Baqi Beg Tarkhan. According to an inscription he was killed in 1570. His tomb was built by his son Isa Khan Tarkhan-II in 1608.
The grave of Jan Baba along with graves of other members of his family are under sheltered baradari type building built over a raised platform, while the womenfolk are buried in a separate chamber in the north-eastern corner. The rectangular building is protected by high walls with a prayer niche in the western wall. Entrance to the monument is provided from the south under a covered baradari type verandah also built on a raised platform.

data.description: It is situated to the north-east of the tomb of Mubarak Khan near the tomb of Jam Nizamuddin in the northern fringe of the Makli Necropolis. The single-domed square building measures 7.5692 x 7.5692 meters. The stone courses on each side rises upto a height of around two meters above ground level and thereafter brick courses follow. It is open on all four sides by lancet-shaped arched openings. A vertical brick lining on either side of the entrance makes two vertical panels. In the present example the corner squinch starts just above the stone course and then a series of pendentives turn the octagon into a circular base for the dome. There is dental basal decoration as a lining below the domical ceiling. According to plaque on the tomb, Malik Raj Paal son of Malik Unar died in 1479 A.D., while an Arabic plaque inside the building gives the whole genealogy of Malik Rajpal, descending from Firozuddin Jam Umar, and thus relating, to a collateral line of Jam Nizamuddin.

Bohi Quba are located about 3.47 kms west of Dakhan on Indus Highway and nearly 30 km north of Shikarpur.Thaheeman-Ja-Quba also known as Bohi Quba belongs to the Thaheems, who historically are known to have fought with the Pathans during the Kalhora period in which Thaheems were martyred. data.description: It is located inside the Makli Hills necropolis of Thatta, to the south of Jani Beg Tarkhan and to the north of Baqi Beg Uzbek tomb enclosures. Among the various unique and imposing structures at Makli Hill, Satcharni is one of the foremost pertinent buildings, which is undoubtedly invites the scholar`s interest in order to solve the mystery regarding the origin of this enigmatic and folkloristic structure. As per local traditions, this building was built for the family of Khusrau Khan Charkas (1555-1613 CE) an eminent figure of Thatta, during the Tarkhan period. As per traditions this enigmatic building has owed its name, which gained tremendous fame, during the succeeding centuries. Khusrau Khan Charkas also constructed a grand mosque known as Masjid-e-Dabgaran or Dabgir Mosque at Thatta in 1588 CE, which is an exquisite precedent, showing the aesthetic sense and engineering skills of the building. Sat, defines seven and Chrurni, means ascending. Another view is that each comer is yielding two stair cases, which obviously means that the present structure is possessing eight stairs cases instead of seven steps. Furthermore, each stair case is accommodating more than eight steps. Therefore, opine that perhaps initially this building was known as Hasht Chrurhni (eight staircases). However, the locals with the passage of time, instead of pronouncing Sha properly, they replaced it with Sa thus, it became as Hast, thus slowly and gradually evolved into Sat, which apparently came to be known as satcharni. Some scholars define it in term of stylistically approach, adopted in this building. They opine that in the lndo-Pak subcontinent, the concept of chamfered plan can be noticed for the first time in the mausoleum of Humayun (1564 CE) was introduced for the first time in the mausoleum of Khusrau Khan Charkas alias Satcharni, which may be dated to the last decade of the 16th century CE. They believe that the amalgamation of various cultural traditions have generally caused for the glorification of the in Satcharni monument. Moreover, the stylistically approach adopted by the masons in its architectural composition has altogether made it a very unique and exquisite specimen of art and architecture in the whole of Makli Hill necropolis.
data.title: Miscellaneous

data.name_of_site: Shahjahani Mosque / Jamia Mosque Thatta Town
data.description: This massive structure is centered around a courtyard measuring 52 x 11.2 m. The prayer chamber on the west is balanced on the east by another chamber of similar size. Both are covered with large domes. On the north and south, two-aisled galleries open by means of arcades on the courtyard. Ninety-three domes cover the entire structure and are probably the cause of a remarkable echo which enables the sermon in the Mihrab to be heart in all parts of the mosque. The mosque contains the most elaborate display of tile-work. The two main chambers in particular are entirely covered with such tiles. The domes are exquisitely laid in a mosaic of radiating blue and white tiles to give an appearance of starry vault. Stylized floral patterns, akin to the 17th century kashi work of Iran decorate the spandrels of the main arches and elsewhere geometrical designs on square tiles. The construction of the mosque was completed by Nawab Abdul Baq Amir Khan on the orders of Shah Jahan.

data.description: It is situated in Gabol village in Barar deh Mirpur Mathelo taluka. Piyaro village is about 12 km in south west of Quba, while Lund Wah is flowing in eastern side about 50 m. Jarwar village is 4 km in south of Quba while Mirpur Mathelo city is 8 km in north west of Quba. It measures 6.70 x 6.70 x 10 m. It is built of burnt bricks, cheroli, and mud mortar. It is square in plan. Entrance is provided from southern side in arch shape, hall of tomb is in square shape from lower side and dome lower part is hexagonal in shape while the upper part is in round shape. Extended rectangular brick work on each side can be seen. Between arches and ventilators, dome is decorated in corbelled arch pattern. Four square arches and four ventilators in dome on hexagonal portion are visible. Most part of the dome is missing. The monument is probably associated to Kalhora period of Sindh.
data.authur_name: Federal Department of Archaeology and Museums, Islamabad.
data.title: Survey and Documentation of Archaeological Sites and Monuments (1995-2001)
data.published_in: Unpublished Survey by Federal Department of Archaeology and Museums

data.description: This tomb is located in Muhammad Khan Vighio village, Nawab Shah. It measures 3.55x3.55x6.50 m. It is square in plan and made of burnt bricks, mud mortar and lime mortar. data.description: This tomb is situated in the Noval Ghori grave yard. This tomb is built with burnt bricks. It has four domes. The tomb has lime plaster all over the walls and domes. Entrance is on northern and southern side in pointed arch shape. There are four blind arches on lower portion and five on upper portion of each side. In center of upper portion, there is arched ventilator on each side. Tomb has a round dome. There are two ventilators on northern and southern side. Its measures 6.70m x 6.70m with maximum height of 8 m. Burnt bricks and mud mortar are construction materials. Tomb is square in plan. Internally, tomb has five arches on upper portion and five on lower side. Eastern and western wall has three blind arches in lower part of wall and two in northern and southern sides. There are four squinch arches in corners of drum. Above squinch, there are two layers of cut bricks. Pendant of the dome has fallen. data.description: Mosque is located in deh Ghouspur; taluka Kand Kot, district Jacobabad. Ghous Pur town is 25 km in west of Kandh Kot city and 65 km in east of Shikarpur city. Entrance is on eastern side with three floral pattern engraved wooden arch doors. In facade, blue glaze tiles are used in upper portion and lower portion has lime plaster. Facade has a series of battlement on top. There is a tower for Azaan in southern corner of courtyard. There are two entrances in courtyard. There are three windows in each northern and southern side of prayer hall. There are two small doors with staircase in western wall. Prayer hall has 9 domes with finials and eight minarets with finials. There are four L shaped thick pillars in center. It measures 20.25 m EW x 20.25 m NS, height: 16 m. Mosque is square in plan. Mosque is decorated with glazed finials, turrets, battlement, arches from outside, while inside is decorated with fresco paintings, golden colour, pendant and wide Mehrab. Inscription is also visible. Internally, there is a wide Mehrab, two arches, two cupboards and two small storing places with wooden door are in western wall. Eastern wall has three wooden doors in arches. Southern wall has three niches with grills. Northern wall has one cupboard, one niche and one door. There are three domes found in row 3 on NS and 3 on EW. East-West domes are painted with blue, pink and white colors. There are four ventilators and four corbelled arches. Cheroli is used on top portion. Central dome is painted with multi-color floral designs. There are 16 small arches above ventilators on central dome. North-south three domes on plain white washed. There are four cemented corbel arches. Central dome has four ventilators and four corbel arches. Blue, pink, yellow and white colors are applied. The monument is probably Associated with Kalhora period of Sindh.

data.name_of_site: Tomb of Hazrat Ghous Hussain Shah Jillani
data.description: Tomb is located in deh Ghouspur, taluka Kandhi Kot, district Jacobabad. It is in the south east side of Jamia mosque of Ghouspur. Ghouspur is 25 km in east of Kandhi Kot city and 65 km in west of Shikarpur. Entrance is on northern side with wooden door. Tomb has four turrets with three finial, one finial of western side turret has fallen. Tomb has one semicircular dome with finial that rests on octagonal drum having three pointed arch panels in rectangular panels in each side of drum. There is a series of battlement on top of drum and on top of walls. Tomb has a courtyard. It measures 9.30 x 9.30 x 15 m. Burnt bricks, cheroli, lime plaster and cement plaster are the construction material. Tomb is square in plan. Tomb is decorated with rectangular and arch panels, battlements, turrets and finials. There is a small Mehrab found in western side. There are three cemented graves of children in western and southern sides of Shah Hussain grave.

data.description: Mosque is located in deh Manjhi, taluka Kandh Kot, district Jacobabad. It is in Gul Muhammad Bajarani village. Tang Wari village is 4 km in north, Jacobabad Kandh Kot Road i.e., called Saiful is 1 km in south. Entrance is on eastern side in wooden door. There are three arches on each side of entrance. There are six arches in each northern and southern side. There are three doors in prayer hall, two windows in each northern and southern side. Prayer hall have three round domes with finials. Mosque has a courtyard; eastern wall of courtyard has seven domes. There are four minarets with finial. Eastern side of courtyard have two rooms of Mujavirs, southern side of Mujavir`s rooms have two arches, northern side has one arch. Mosque has a verandah; its northern and southern sides have 5 arches on each side. Mosque measures 16.70 x 15 x 13 m. Burnt bricks, mud bricks, mud mortar and lime plaster are construction materials. Mosque is rectangular in plan. Mosque is decorated with arches minarets and floral paintings. Internally, roof of prayer hall and Mujawir`s room are surviving, some portions of verandah roof is fallen. Drum have blind arches, two arches separate domes. This mosque exists in miserable condition.

data.description: This tomb lies in the Sui Sharif village. The Tahir Bhatti village is at few meters distance in the south. The Tig Shah village is at 1 km distance in the north. The Muhammad Pur village lies at 2 km distance in the west. This tomb is located at 12 km distance in the south west corner of Ubaro city. The tomb has square plan, it has four major minarets on all four sides. The tomb has a big dome. The dome has octagonal drum with eight minarets and eight ventilators. The tomb has two entrances from eastern and northern side. Tomb is existing in good condition. It measures 9 x 9 x 17 m. It is made of burnt bricks, cement mortar and plaster is used in the renovation. The tomb has massive thick walls all four sides. There is a courtyard with roof around all four sides to the tomb. The tomb has glazed tiles work on and inside the tomb, beautiful mirror decorative work has also been done. There are total eight graves inside the tomb. There is a Mehrab towards the western side. The monument is probably associated to Kalhoro period of Sindh.

data.description: Shrine is located in deh, taluka and district Jacobabad. It is edge of Quetta-Shikarpur Road. data.description: Tomb is located in deh Murad Ali, taluka Garhi Khairo, district Jacobabad. Rehan Khan Jamali village is in the north, Garhi Khairo city is about 8 km in the northwest, and Junejo Railway Station is about 3 km in south. Entrance is on southern side in arch shape door, above the door is a rectangular panel, above it, there is an arch with crown. Both sides of the door have three rectangular panels having blind arches. Eastern, western and northern side has five blind arches in three rows. There is a series of battlement on top of walls. Tomb has octagonal drum; dome is round with broken finial and lotus flower. Burnt bricks, mud mortar; lime plaster and cheroli are the construction materials. Tomb is square in plan and decorated with rectangular panels, blind arches, crown finial, lotus flower from outside, while inside, it is decorated with blind arches, color paintings and squinch arches. Internally, eastern wall has one large size arch and two small arches on each wall. Dome rests on octagonal drum, which has 16 blind arches and four squinch arches in corners. There are different scenes of animals, painted with multicolor on wall. Tomb is existing in miserable condition and probably belongs to Kalhora period of Sindh.

data.description: Fort of Talpur period is situated in deh Sadhooja taluka Moro district Naushero Feroz. In east of Kot Nather detho wali and in north west is Goth Mobeyja, Naushero is 11 km in north and Moro is 13 km in south. At present fort is occupied by the Burraro community and inside the courtyard they have built their houses. It is rectangular in plan. Main entrance is provided from east side. There are 4 watch towers in all corners. There is no bastion in center of wall for support from inside or outside. There is a round shape stupa or crown stage in the center of courtyard of fort. From the stupa of courtyard, many t/c bricks or tiles found by the villagers, with the impression of human and floral motif and a t/c scale with the impression of 24 blocks of holes.

data.description: This mosque is situated in goth Darbelo deh Darbhro taluka Kandiyaro district Naushero Feroz. It is rectangular in plan. Entrance from eastern side is provided with three arch shape doors while two windows in north and south side. There are eight small minarets with turret on eastern wall of prayer hall while a series of battlement on verandah and prayer hall. Mosque is mainly decorated with glazed tiles and turrets. Arabic and Persian inscription can be seen on tiles, some Persian poetry, names and date of repairing on tiles is also evident. Prayer hall is divided into three portions, central portion is wider than others. There is a Mehrab in center of Qibla wall while two niches are on corner of Mehrab. From inside there are blind arches and rectangular panels. There are three domes, each dome has four squinch arches while a ventilator in central dome. With squinches there are four blind arches in hexagonal portion.

data.description: This mosque is situated in goth and deh Dhingo, taluka Bhiria district Naushero Feroz. It is rectangular in plan and the main entrance is provided from eastern side. Only the ruins of main entrance in arch shape door and glazed tiles decoration work on main entrance is preserved. There are two small pillars with glazed turret are still surviving. Prayer hall of mosque is small. Only the western wall with mihrab and small portion of northern and southern wall are remaining now. There is a blind arch and rectangular panels on western wall from inside. Decoration in the mosque is done with glazed tiles, turrets and blind arches and Persian inscription on main entrance. There are two types of bricks used in construction in prayer hall, mud bricks in hall and burnt bricks in foundation.

data.description: This fort of mud walls is situated in village Jawan Shah deh Dhiongo, taluka Bhiria in district Naushero Feroz. At present fort is surrounded by agricultural land from all sides; also from inside. Fort is square in plan. Main entrance is provided from eastern side. There are four watch towers in each corner of fort, while a wall in front of main entrance for shade or a reception or guard room in front of main entrance is provided. The fort is in ruined condition. Only the walls of fort are present and associated to Talpur period of Sindh.

data.description: This mosque is situated in Syed Mohallah deh Khai Maman, taluka Bhiria in district Naushero Feroz.  Mosque is built of burnt bricks, mud bricks, lime mortar and mud mortar. Brick size is 45 x 23 x 6 cm. Mosque is square in plan. Entrance of mosque is totally disappeared. Only the ruins of northern, southern and western walls with mihrab are visible. In southern wall, there is a pointed arch. Mehrab have lime plaster and painting with multi color. There is no dome or roof on prayer hall, only the squinch arches are visible in badly damaged condition. Some portion of dome are visible.

data.description: This tomb is situated in Syed Mohallah adjacent to the Jamia mosque of Noor Muhammad Shah Mosque. Tomb is built of burnt bricks, lime mortar, mud mortar and glazed tiles. Tomb is square in plan. Main entrance is provided from southern side only with multi cusp arch. After renovation, facade have modern glazed tiles, cement and glass work. There are minarets on facade; each minaret has a canopy and lotus flower with glazed turrets. A series of crowns is present on the top of facade. There is round dome sits on hexagonal drum with eight small turrets on drum while a finial with lotus flower on top. Four squinch arches are supporting the drum of dome. While four ventilators between squinches are also evident. Pendant is also evident in the center of drum. Outstanding floral, geometrical, marble and glazed tile work on outside and inside of tomb is visible. Only old inscription in Persian on grave head stone showing date 1207 A.H. There are blind arches and rectangular panels on the walls of the tomb.

data.description: This site is located at a distance of 1km in west of deh Ghittan wan, taluka Rohri and district Sukkur. The same site is also locally known with the name of Kinhari. The is a temporary settlement or camping ground is situated on sand dunes. Potshards in abundance are spread all over the surface in vast area. Site itself is totally abandoned; serves as grazing field for animals. The kachha track passes through the site which is in use of villagers. Wild vegetation is also dotted on surface throughout the remains area. The red ware pottery fragments found on the surface having cut mark, potters mark, incised lines, stamped and relief design on outside while red ware shards painted in black in net design and parallel bands are also found. Grey ware rims having cutmarks; potters identification marks are also visible on few shards. Besides pottery, chert blades are also visible on the surface.

data.description: This archeological mound is located in the Ghotki District, taluka Deharki, deh Sucharo. Noohindri Dara is about 4 km in its west, Muhammad Shah Ji Bhit is about 1 12 km in its east, while Lune Waro Daro is about 4 km in its south. The prehistoric mound is situated in the desert. It is spread over a large area, modern graveyard is present over the center of the mound. Pottery is scattered on the surface of site. This site is extended over 700 m from east to west and in breath is 500 m from north to south, its height is 15 m approximately. The pottery of this site is found in dull red ware with medium in texture. Plain incised and monochrome painted body shards are visible on the surface. Few grey ware shards are also observed. In other finds, complete small T/C bead and very small T/C ball are also included. The site is probably associated to Neolithic period.

data.description: It is one of the most notable buildings of Karachi. It was constructed in 1863 to commemorate the long and brilliant administration of Sir Bartle Frere when he was called back to the Viceroy`s Council in 1859. The Hall is in the Venetian Gothic style with an octagonal tower crowned with iron cage. It is built with yellowish limestone of Jungshahi. The columns and arches of the wide verandahs are exceedingly graceful and the whole details are pleasing. The upper spire let is 44 m above ground level. data.description: The site is situated along the western side of a small sand dune located along cultivated lands. This is a huge settlement with thick density of cultural assemblage scattered over the surface. The surface is literary look red from quite a distance. The tops surface and entire western side of a small sand dune is covered with artifacts mainly the pottery. The concentration of objects in cluster shape suggests the separate hut/house. In northern side some outlines of the rooms on the surface were noticed. These rooms might have been constructed with mud wall at base and roof with wooden material. This architectural tradition is commonly exercised in surrounding area. This site is very rich in cultural material such as pottery in various sizes and decorated with different designs and motifs; glass pieces, bangles, coin and iron pieces. Several bones were also observed on the surface. The preliminary examination of artifacts suggests the date from 8th to 11th Century AD.

data.description: The site of Taloor-ji Bhit is situated ten km in northeast of Kot Lalo. The site measures as total of 443 m East-West and 467 m North-South and cover a total of 206881sq.m area. The site is divided into two portions designated as (A) mounded and (B) surface scatter. The mounded part of site is located on the west side within alluvial plain area and consists of at least two mounds elevated almost three m in height from the ground surface areas. The second part; i.e., surface scatter, is situated on the sand dune at least 02 to 04 m higher from the surrounded plains. This is a very large site occupied during the Kot Dijian period and continued until the Indus period. The robber`s ditch was examined closely and several Kot Dijian objects were found, however the entire site is densely covered with Indus period artifact.
data.title: Kot Dijian Settlements in Alluvial Plains and Desert of Sindh

The limestone blocks were found in large quantity in various parts of the site indicating limestone used for house construction. The different stratigraphic layers were observed in the burrows where the cultural material was embedded in the section, showing different occupation levels, where from some Kot Dijian period shards were collected.

data.description: This site lies at a low-lying area sloping towards south, located in the south of Wadi Sim (Lake) and east of Bakri Waro where there is the Vakar Valley in the south. The lakes and alluvial valley make diverse subsistence resource bases. The site is very rich in the cultural material. The collection of several stone tools including many types of points, core and flakes are important. Majority of the tools are very small like geometric tools of the Mesolithic period. Pottery is mainly plain and is associated with various periods; for example, the hand-built and grit mixed pottery belong to the Hakra period and the short neck wheel-turned pottery shows affinity with the Kot Dijian period. Besides this cultural assemblage, terracotta cakes, terracotta bangles, shell objects and one sandstone polisher were also collected. The viscosity of scattered cultural material suggests that this site might have been occupied for a long time period and cannot be a campsite of nomads.

data.description: The site occupies north-western side of the Phariaro town and lies on the flat top of a sand dune. The cultural material, which sparsely scattering on the surface, belongs to different periods suggesting seasonal halt of nomads. Nearby there is a dry lake, locally called Manchhar Lake, which is presently under cultivation. The site yielded plain, painted and incised pottery as well as Chert flakes and glass embroidery mirrors. It can be associated with Hakra, 4th millennium BC, and subsequent historic periods down to modern times.

data.description: The site lies on the south-western of Phariaro town and occupies the southern slopes of a sand dune. data.description: The site is located two km south of Deariro village in Deh Mamro, Taluka Saleh Pat on the flat alluvial ground elevating almost five m from surrounding area. The site occupies southern side of the sand dunes and has open valley in front. The valley is dominated by Khaber plants. The site consists of a mound some two m above the surrounding area. The brunt brick fragment is dispersed all over the site. Brick robbers have destroyed some portions of the site. There no any visible features were recorded. Thus, the brunt brick suggested some permanent structures constructed here in this settlement. The cultural objects include pottery, chert stone, sand stone, shell bead, twisted copper rod and iron pieces. The discovery of iron pieces indicates re-habituate of the area during Iron Age as these people were settled just half km away from this settlement.
data.title: Recent Research at Harappan Settlements along the Ancient Hakra  River

data.description: The site is located in the valley on the small sand dune or the raised place covering a total of 170x65x2 m area. The long axis is in the north/south direction. On the surface of site several hearths, vitrified slag, and thick concentration of pottery, T/C cakes and other cultural objects were noticed. The semiprecious beads, shell bangles and white disk beads were also found from surface. No any baked brick was noticed and/or recorded that have possibly suggested for the utilization of permanent material for residential structures. Nevertheless, the density of cultural material scattered on the surface actually indicated that this was a permanent village entirely made of thatches; however, there might have been some mud wall at the base. During surface analysis of the site, traces of mud structures were observed for example, almost at the center of site the traces of mud wall in square shape were present.
data.title: Recent Research at Harappan Settlements along the Ancient Hakra  River

data.description: This mosque is located in village and deh Bahadurpur, taluka Thul, district Jacobabad. Main entrance has one door in pointed arch while arch portion is painted with multi-colours geometrical patterns. Above pointed arch, there are two large rectangular panels. Top of the wall have two turrets with finial in each corner. Series of merlons and a semi-circular dome on octagonal drum having series of merlons. Mosque has three doors in eastern wall of prayer hall and one door in each northern and southern wall. There are six arches in eastern and western wall and two in each northern and southern wall. Prayer hall have three domes rests on octagonal drum. There are four ventilators in each drum. There is a series of merlons on top of drum. Facade has green paint (out living the top). There is a space for Azaan in eastern side. Mosque consists of prayer hall, verandah and courtyard and all the structures are plastered with lime. Burnt bricks, mud mortar, mud plaster, lime plaster and cement are constructions materials. Mosque is decorated with pointed arch, rectangular panels, battlements, turrets, finial, multi-color geometrical patterns, green oil paint and floral paintings. Internally, there is a Mehrab having floral painting in western wall. There are three blind arches on each side of Mehrab. There are two blind arches with door are present in both northern and southern side. There are three domes, central dome is plain and plastered with mud mortar, central drum have eight ventilators and below it there are eight arches. Northern drum has four ventilators and eight arches, southern drum has three ventilators and eight arches. There are two open arches in northern side, two in southern side and six in eastern side, for entrance. Mosque is probably associated to Kalhora period of Sindh.

data.description: This mosque is located in village and deh Zangipur, taluka Thul, district Jacobabad. Dil Murad Railway Station is about 4 km in south-east, Thul Town is 24 km in west. Main entrance is on eastern side with three wooden doors, there are several rectangular and arch panels having geometrical pattern, blue glaze tiles on eastern side. Northern, southern and western sides have three rows of rectangular panels, top row have five horizontal rectangular panels while lower two rows have fine vertical rectangular panel having arch panel in each row. There are three semicircular domes with finials, central dome is larger then other domes. Domes rests on octagonal drum. There is a series of battlement. Eastern wall has four turrets with finials. Internally, western wall has a Mehrab having blue glaze tiles and Persian inscription, there is one blind arch on each side of Mehrab. Prayer hall and domes are decorated with multicolor paintings. Central dome has twelve arches on upper portion and six on lower portion. Central dome has mirror work. There are four open ventilators and four closed ventilators. Prayer hall is divided into three portions. Northern and southern walls have two blind arches and a niche or door. Eastern wall has two blind arches and doors. Eastern room have niches, doors, blind arches and ventilators.

data.description: Mosque is located in deh Ghouspur; taluka Kand Kot, district Jacobabad. Ghous Pur town is 25 km in west of Kandh Kot city and 65 km in east of Shikarpur city. Entrance is on eastern side with three floral pattern engraved wooden arch doors. In facade, blue glaze tiles are used in upper portion and lower portion has lime plaster. Facade has a series of battlement on top. There is a tower for Aza`an in southern corner of courtyard. There are two entrances in courtyard. There are three windows in each northern and southern side of prayer hall. There are two small doors with staircase in western wall. Prayer hall has 9 domes with finials and eight minarets with finials. There are four L shaped thick pillars in center. Present structures measures 20.25 x 20.25 x 16m. Mosque is square in plan. Mosque is decorated with glaze finials, turrets, battlement, arches from outside, while inside is decorated with fresco paintings, golden colour, pendant and wide Mehrab. Inscription is also visible. Internally, there is a wide Mehrab, two arches, two cupboards and two small storing places with wooden door are in western wall. Eastern wall has three wooden doors in arches. Southern wall has three niches with grills. Northern wall has one cupboard, one niche and one door. There are three domes found in row 3 on North-South and 3 on East-West. East-West domes are painted with blue, pink and white colors. There are four ventilators and four corbelled arches. Cheroli is used on top portion. Central dome is painted with multi-color floral designs. There are 16 small arches above ventilators on central dome. North-south three domes on plain white washed. There are four cemented corbel arches. Central dome has four ventilators and four corbel arches. Blue, pink, yellow and white colors are applied. The monument is probably associated with Mughal period of Sindh.

data.description: This unidentified building is located in deh Ghouspur, taluka Kandhkot, district Jacobabad. It is in north-west of Jamia Mosque of Ghouspur. Kandh Kot town is 25 km in east, Shikarpur city is about 65 km in west. This is a double story building. There are six blind arches and six rectangular panel in (N-S) north-southern wall, while (E-W) east-western wall has two blind arches and one rectangular panel. There is a stair-case in southern side. Roof is fallen, only remains of beams are present. There are two rooms in the building, one in northern side and other in southern side. Present structures measures 17.80 x 6.10 x 5 m. Burnt bricks, mud bricks and mud mortar are the construction materials. This building is rectangular in plan. This building decorated with blind arches, rectangular panels and niches. It exists in ruined condition and probably associated with Kalhora dynasty of Sindh.

data.description: Mosque is located in village and deh Jan Muhammad, taluka Kashmore, district Jacobabad. Bakhshah Pur is in south-east, shah wah is about 12 km in north. Haji Noor Din is in the west, Kahsmore is about 24 km in the east. Two pillars support main entrance, above these pillars are minarets with finial and in between these pillars, there is grill having birds and geometrical designs. There are three doors in prayer hall. Front portion of prayer hall have two large and two small turrets with finials. There is a series of battlement and crown on top of eastern wall of prayer hall. Floor of the mosque was renovated 20 years ago. It measures 16 m x 12 m x 15 m. Burnt bricks, lime plaster, cheroli, glaze tiles are construction materials. Mosque is rectangular in plan and decorated with Quranic verses and Persian inscription on eastern and western wall and on roof. Mosque is also decorated with turrets, finials, crowns, geometrical and birds pattern screen, battlements, glaze tiles. It exists in good condition and probably associated with Kalhora period of Sindh.

data.description: Tomb is located in deh Rasoolabad, taluka Garhi Khairo, district Jacobabad. Tomb is in the south of village Dad Muhammad Khan Lohar. Begair canal is in the south, Garhi Khairo town is 6 km in the west, Illahi Bux village is about 100 m in the south west. Entrance is on eastern side with one wooden door having floral pattern engravings above the door there are two large blind arches, decorated with glaze tiles. There is Persian inscription above the door. There are two rectangular panels on each side of door. Northern, southern and western sides have blind arches in fine rows. Tomb has a semicircular dome with glaze turrets, it rests on hexagonal drum, there are ten blind arches with tiles and grills on drum. Tomb is decorated with rectangular panels, blind arches with tiles and grills on drum. Burnt bricks, glaze tiles, lime plaster and mud mortar are construction materials. Tomb is square in plan and decorated with rectangular panels, blind arches, turrets and glazed tiles. Above the door, there is a Kalima and Persian inscription. Internally, dome has floral fresco paintings. There are four arches in corners decorated with fresco painting. Hall has plain walls. There is one ventilator in eastern wall, and two windows in northern and southern side. There are four graves in the tomb. Head stone of three graves have Persian inscription.

data.description: This archaeological mound is situated in village Ali Nawaz Jalbani, deh Jalbani, taluka Garhi Khairo, and district Jacobabad. Other places, which are located in the surrounding of the mound, are Miro Khan, Ghari Khairo road is on the edge of site on southern side, and Garhi Khairo city is about 7 km in its south. This site is divided into different small mounds, pottery is scattered on the surface of mound. This site is extended over 125 m from east to west and in breath is 95 m from north to south and its height is 6 m approximately. The pottery of this site is found in dull red ware with medium and thin in texture and all are in plain. Pottery mostly found in variation of body shards, plates, dish with base, rim and lid, one light grooved body shards and vitrified body shards are also found.

Chang village is in the south, Rahimabd Wah is in the west, Jacobabad city is 16 km from Dad Dari village. Main entrance is on eastern side. Northern and southern sides have one window on each side. data.description: This mosque is situated in the Saduja village. This mosque lies 11 km north of Moro city, 13 km south of Naushehro Feroz. This mosque is built with burnt bricks, has three domes with finials, and four minarets over the top. The minarets are existing along with finial. The mosque has an eastern entrance. The facade has 3 blind arches into the squire panels. It is rectangular in plan. The mosque has an eastern main entrance. The facade has four minarets. There are two small windows right and left side of the main entrance. There are three domes with round drum, the drum has eight small blind arches inside. There are two windows, one to north, other on the southern side in big blind arched. The Mehrab is also built in a large blind arch. The prayer hall has two large arched beams which support the roof. The mosque exit in preserved condition and probably associated to Talpur dynasty of Sindh.

data.description: This tomb is situated in the Kacha area of Gacharo village. It is situated at short distance in the south of Izzat Khan Bughio village and 8 km in the south west of Moro. This tomb is built with burnt bricks. It has a dome with finial. There are six minarets on the tomb. The minarets are also exists with finials. The tomb has main entrance from southern side but it has another entrance from northern side. Presently the renovation work is being done. Burnt bricks, cement and lime plaster is used in construction. The facade has beautiful floral work. There is a main entrance from northern side. Facade has 4 minarets. There is a rectangular courtyard on the front side. The courtyard has a graveyard. The building is standing inward on the top. Geometrical, floral and tile work is clear. There are five graves inside the tomb; the large one grave is of the Saint. There is a Mehrab in the southern wall. Dome is round inside with eight corner arches. Floral and geometrical work is done inside the dome. There are three large blind arches on all three walls except the eastern. The tomb is completely renovated.

data.description: Tomb is situated in deh and taluka Moro district Nausharo Feroz. National Highway is in west of tomb is about 150 m while the Moro city is in north of tomb. Tomb is square in plan. This tomb is situated beside the national highway and 1 km in south of Moro city. The tomb is standing in the Chuttan Shah grave yard. This tomb is built with burnt bricks. It has a round dome with finial. Tomb has a northern arched entrance. It has mud plaster. The tomb has an arched entrance from northern side. The facade has no remarkable structure. There are two others entrance southern and eastern side but presently not in use. There is a graveyard in its surrounding. The tomb has Mehrab into a large blind arch. Beside the Mehrab there are two niches. The other three side wall has the same features. Dome is round. There are 4 blind arches and 4 squinch arches on the drum. There are 4 graves inside the tomb and existing in very miserable condition. Tomb is probably associated to Kalhora period of Sindh.

data.description: This mosque is situated as the Shaikh Mohallah of Moro city. This also situated at a short distance in the south of Ahmed Shah School. This mosque is built with brunt bricks along with lime mortar. The mosque has three domes. The central dome is larger one, it has a small finial. There are octagonal drums on the dome. There are six minarets on the mosque. It measures 12m x 6.25m with a height of 11m and rectangular in plan. The mosque has an eastern entrance into a large blind arch, there are two windows to the right and left side of the main entrance. The facade has two small minarets. There is a newly built courtyard which has 5 entrances into the multi-cusped arches. The top of the courtyard has a row battlement. Internally mosque has one central round dome and two half domes. The central dome has floral work in emboss. The drum has 4 multi-cusped squinch arches and four ventilators. The half dome has two squinch arches and 3 blind aches. There are two large blind arches on the eastern and western wall. Two windows on each side wall. Floor is made of square burnt  bricks. The monument is associated with Talpur period of Sindh.

data.description: This mosque is situated in the Haji Musa Rajpar village. It is 2 km south of Shahija and about 200 m in west of Naushera Feroz Padidan road and about 3 in the south of Naushero Feroz city. This mosque is built with burnt bricks. It has three entrances from eastern sides for the courtyard and one entrance to the prayer hall. The domes survive with finial and octagonal drums. It measures  4.70m E-W x 7.90m NS and its maximum height is 9 m. Burnt bricks, lime mortar, plaster and mud mortar are used in the construction. Bricks size is 30 x 15 x 7cm. Facade has three entrances for the mosque and to minarets type small turrets on the top. Mosque has 3 domes over the courtyard and one large dome over the prayer hall. The facade has series of squire and arched panels. The mosque has a row of battlements on the western, northern and southern sides. There is a newly built terrace. There are stairs for the roof on the right side of the mosque. The roof of the courtyard has corbelled and blind arches all sides. There is a calligraphic round plate in the center of the dome. The drum of the dome has 4 squinch arches and 4 blind arches. There are four large blind arches and niches in the prayer hall. The prayer hall has small entrance given into large blind arch.

data.description: This mosque is situated in the Fazal Mohammad village, left side on the Tharo Shah Mithiani road. It is 1 km in the west of Muhammad Maussa village and 3 km in the west of Tharo Shah and 10 km in the north of Naushero Feroz. This mosque is built with burnt bricks. It has one round dome with finial and six turrets. The mosque has an eastern entrance and five small archly windows. The facade has a large cusped blind arch over the main entrance and two small cusped arches into a rectangular panel over the windows. The mosque has a small eastern entrance into a large cusped blind arch, two windows in the cusped arches and 4 turrets on the facade. There is a row of battlements on the top. Lime plaster has been applied all over the mosque. The dome is in round shape with octagonal drum. There is a courtyard in front of the mosque. It also has a square burnt bricks floor. Internally mosque has painted round dome with 3 archly ventilators and 4 squinch arches. There are two other half domes, on right and left side of the mosque. It has 2 squinch arches, one blind arch to each. Mehrab is built in a large blind arch. The Mehrab is cusped arched. There are four two niches on the western wall. There are two arched windows on right and left side of the mosque. The eastern wall has an entrance into a large blind arch.

data.description: This shrine is situated in the Sakhi Daood Wahi village. It is 1 km in west of Saeed Khan Lund village, 12 km in the north of Muhammad Sulaiman Dehrai, 2 km in the south of Safi Muhammad village and 15 km in the north of Naushero Feroz. This tomb or shrine is built with burnt bricks. It has 4 turrets and 9 round domes with finial. The tomb       rectangular panels to the walls and octagonal drum with 8 turrets. The tomb has a southern entrance through a beautiful series. The tomb has a beautiful wood carved door and square in plan. The tomb has eight turrets on the drum of the dome. There is a mosque attached to the facade side (eastern). The main entrance is provided through a Sarai from southern side. There is a row of battlements all corners. The drum has six blind arches. There is grave yard all four sides and other building. There are 3 graves inside the tomb. The larger one is of the grave of the saint. There are double panels of the blind arches into a large blind arch on all four sides of the tomb. The floor has floral glazed tiles. The tomb is associated with Kalhora dynasty of Sindh.

data.description: This mosque is situated in Side Mohallah (Khateeb Mohallah) in deh taluka and district Naushero Feroz. Main entrance is from east side with three arch shape doors. On eastern wall of prayer hall there are blind arches and rectangular panels while a series of battlement on facade. There are four small minarets with glazed turrets on eastern wall of prayer hall. There are three large size domes with glaze finial standing on hexagonal base. Multi-color glazed tiles have been used on eastern wall while Persian inscription is found on tiles of eastern wall. data.description: This mosque is situated in village and deh ghangno taluka in district Naushero Feroz. It is rectangular in plan. The main entrance from eastern side with three arch shape doors while one door in northern and one in southern side is provided. There are three large size blind arches and rectangular panels on facade. A stair case is in northern corner leads to top of roof. There is a series of battlement on top of eastern wall. Four turrets on eastern wall while crown is present in between the turrets. There are three domes with glazed finial. There are 6 niches in eastern and six in western wall while two in northern and two in southern sides. There is Mehrab in center of Qibla wall. Prayer hall is divided into three portions with multi-cusp arches. There are 4 squinch arches supported domes with 4 ventilators.

data.description: This mosque is situated in new Darbalo village, deh Dubrho taluka Bhiria in district Naushero Feroz, half km from Darbalo Police Station and 100 m away from Rural Health Centre. It is rectangular in plan. Entrance is provided from eastern side with three arch shaped doors. All three doors are in large blind arches. On eastern wall of prayer hall there are four glazed turrets. There is a glazed tile decoration on the front facade and northern and southern sides. Mosque is mainly decorated with glazed turrets, tiles, finials and Persian inscription. From inside Mehrab is in Qibla wall while two niches on both corner of Mehrab, size is equal to Mehrab. There are two windows on southern and northern sides. On each wall there are blind arches and rectangular panels. There are three domes supported by squinch arches in each dome while small blind arches in center of squinch. Mosque was built in 1310 A.H. and renovated time to time.

data.description: This mosque is situated in village and deh Dali, taluka Bhiria, District Naushero Feroz. It is built of burnt bricks, mud mortar, lime mortar, mud bricks, and glazed tiles. Mosque is rectangular in plan. Main entrance is provided from eastern side with three arch shape doors while two doors in north and south side each. On facade glazed tile work is visible in series. A new modern verandah in front prayer hall is added. While four minarets and seven turrets on facade are also visible. There are blind arches on wall, prayer hall is divided into three portions central portion is wider than others. There is a mihrab in center of Qibla wall while two niches equal size of Mehrab in Qibla wall. There are three domes with glazed finials; each dome has 4 squinch arches and 4 ventilators. Drum is round and base of dome is hexagonal. Drum have pendant and painting in center. Mosque is probably associated to Talpur period of Sindh.

data.description: The site Is located 2km in west of village & deh Sangrar, taluka Rohri and district Sukkur. The site is on natural sand dunes, but forming a sizeable portion of the mound. The pattern of potshards on the site area and its orientation, nature and composition of artifacts clearly represents the site as a camping ground where as the T.C shards are thickly distributed all over the surface of site. A newly constructed mosque along with a house are the only infrastructures of noticeable feature standing on the nearby area while widely grown bushes cover the hole land scape. Surface collection from the site clearly recommend that the site was occupied as a camp between 13th - 15th century CE.

data.description: The site is located approximately 2km South east of the government primary school Poonger Bhanbhro and north of the Miano Gas Field Taluka Saleh Pat, district Sukkur. The site is in oblong shape measured as300 m in length in North south direction and 150 m in east west having approximately 2 m total height from surrounding grounds. The majority part is as surface scatter. It has sand dunes from all three directions through which the Hakra River was flowing. A thick layer of cultural material mainly brick pieces is present over the surface. The scattered artifacts are spread in approximately 45000 sq. m area.
data.title: Archaeology and Ethno-archaeology of Poonger Bhanbhro Settlement of Indus Civilization

data.description: The site is located on the low-lying sand dune. Scattered cultural material was recorded on the top surface of sand dune which does not exceed eight m height from surrounding plains. It has the Nara valley on east and north directions while the sand dunes continue in west and south directions. The cultural material was present in clusters suggesting separate huts. The viscosity of objects presents on the surface indicated that nomads occupied this spot frequently throughout various periods. From this site, pottery in various shapes, sizes, and decoration, chert flakes and glass pieces ere documented. The cultural material shows similarities with various periods for example Hakra, Indus and Historic periods.
data.title: Archaeological Survey of Nawabshah Sand Dunes Along Ancient Hakra River Of Thar Desert Of Sindh, Pakistan

data.description: The thin scatter of cultural object was noticed on the slopes of a small sand dune along southern sides where a cluster of at least three lakes was present running parallel to each other. These lakes are narrow strips with maximum length of one km in North south direction. These lakes must have provided best subsistence resources which were utilized for seasonally. The thin presence of objects also suggests that this spot was occupied for short time period and hence is called as a camp site. The thin scatter of cultural material did not provided diversity of object but few potshards of different size suggesting different type of utensil for daily life; the flakes of chert stone suggesting manufacture of stone implements. The pottery showed characteristics of Hakra period.
data.title: Archaeological Survey of Nawabshah Sand Dunes Along Ancient Hakra River Of Thar Desert Of Sindh, Pakistan

data.description: The site is located in Deh Rajpar, Taluka Kot Diji, district Khairpur and about 12; km northwest of the present village of Khannan Buraro, and about 01 km east of pump station No.33. This settlement is situated at the distance of three (05) km from Rohri hills near Adhm Sultan ja Quba and seven km northeast of Kot Diji site (Shaikh 1995, Laghari 1990). The site consists of two small mounds designated as A and measures as 49x45 m and B measures as 42x41 m and raise at height about 1 m from surround agricultural lands. On the mound A; tomb of saint is built and is thus saved from further destruction. However, the mound B might have been leveled for agricultural purposes. From this site, the Kot Dijian and Indus period pottery, terracotta cakes, bangles, chert flakes, blades, and core and grinding stone were collected.
data.title: Kot Dijian Settlements in Alluvial Plains and Desert of Sindh

data.description: The site is situated on the flat top of the eastern part of the same sand dune. At the base of this dune in eastern side, a brackish water lake of Bakri Waro is present. The banks of lake are covered with various types of plants and bushes very suitable for game and domesticated animals like cattle, and goat etc. The site consists of surface scatter where artifacts are scattered in good quantity over vast area. A 4x4 m trench was laid to know the subsurface continuity of cultural deposits; area was excavated a half a meter depth but nothing was found. The excavation is sand is very difficult because of the loose sand only monsoon season would be best pick of archaeologists in terms of deep excavation. Another alternative is to apply tremendous amount of water and maintain moisture in the sand which was not possible for me at moment. The cultural material includes potshards and micro flaking. A good number of flint geometric tool were collected. The object depository form site consists of chert implements including blade, pointed tools, triangles, medial blade, arrow head, copper pieces, shell bangles, terracotta figurine, terracotta bangles, stone bead, white disc beads, and other objects.
data.title: Recent Archaeological Discoveries in Sindh Pakistan
data.published_in: Linguistics, Archaeology and the Human Past (2008)

data.description: Thariri Iban Odho is situated in Deh Noorgah Unar, Taluka Garhi Yasin, District Shikarpur. The site is visible and accessible just off the main road of Shaikarpur to Ratodero, close to the village Iban Odho, 10-km South West of Garhi Yasin town. Because of agricultural activity around the site, we have been unable to demark its extension but the existing mound measures as 172 m in length, N/S and 115 m in width, E/W direction with total height about 16 m from surrounding ground level. During the surface analysis of this site several important features like kilns and wall and cultural objects were recorded (Kazi & Mallah1991). The cultural objects include vase, bowl, jar, large storage/container, Miniature pots, perforated cylinder jars, plates and dish on stands. The other Terracotta object are female figurine, bull cart frames, cart wheels, bangles, beads, terracotta cakes, balls and animal figurine. The marine shell bangles and stone objects were part of collection. The stone objects include sandstone polisher, chert blade core, flakes, hammers and chert drill. The presence of marine shell bangles, chert stone, and sandstone certain suggest some interaction with surrounding regions.
data.title: Recent Archaeological Discoveries in Sindh Pakistan
data.published_in: Linguistics, Archaeology and the Human Past (2008)
