data.name_of_site: Mir Ghulam Ali Khan Talpur Palace
data.description: The palace is situated in Mir Ghulam Ali Town, Taluka Matli. It can be accessed from Matli Bypass- Tando Ghulam Ali link road. Mir Ghulam Ali Khan Talpur palace complex is enclosed within a boundary wall with main gate. Inside the boundary wall, there are seven structures: the main palace, Haveli, three mud structures, kitchen and prayer area. Architectural details of Structure-01 (Palace), Structure-01, the palace is a double-storey building with a courtyard enclosed within a wall (recent). The palace is constructed with burnt bricks. The facade of the palace has six semi-circular arched entrances within wooden Jafri doors and three arched windows. The facade is adorned with Kashi tiles within circular frames. There is a cornice border with Kashi border on the ground and 1st floor.

data.description: Mandhivo Gad Sheri Lourang Dave is located in Taluka Matli, district Badin. it lies about 01 km north-east of Shah Deewano village. It can be accessed from Matli-Tando Ghulam Ali road. It is a burial place with canopy inside the enclosed wall which belongs to a Hindu, though Hindus do not bury but cremate, in this case Mandhivo Gad Sheri Lourang Dave was buried. Hindus visit this burial place and look after it.
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: Daveri Jo Daro lies about 08 km south-west of Tando Ghulam Ali town, near Ghail Pur village. Daveri Jo Daro has a huge concentration of cultural material, scattered on the surface which included plain pottery, painted black on red ware, terracotta quern, animal figurines, bricks and brick bats. Similar cultural material has been found at Badin sites chronologically bracketed between 12th to 18th century CE. The cultural material was in a very fragile condition.
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: Talpur graveyard is located near Lund village, it can be accessed from Shadi Large town which lies about 05 km to the south-west via Badin-Naukot road. The graveyard belongs to Manikani and Bijrani Talpurs (Manik and Bijar Khan both were brothers and sons of Mir Suleman Khan), the Manikani Talpurs ruled Mirpur Khas and descended from Mir Manik. The graveyard is in a ruined condition and encroached by locals. Presently the remains of two canopies and some old and recent graves are surviving. Both canopies are ruined, the super structure of the canopies had collapsed and lying beside the graves. Both canopies were originally constructed with yellow carved stones and erected on a double platform. There were two graves in the first canopy, one grave belonged to Waliya Talpur whereas the second grave was also with a name but not legible.
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: Halu -jo- Daro is located in village Saindad Khoso near Dost Ali pull, it can be accessed from Qamber-Shahdadkot link road to Halu-jo-Daro. The Archaeological site of Halu -jo- Daro is a small sized mound. Its measurements are 60 m in length, 53 m in breadth and height is 2.7 m from surrounding. The local people mentioned the site to have been once a rich site, but its present condition does not portray any such evidence, some cultural material was found by villagers. Cultural material included complete parts of terracotta quern and pieces of stone grinder and one potsherd. Some traces of structural evidences of burnt bricks were present on the mound. The site due to presence of limited cultural material was not identified but the material with the villagers renders it to be Islamic period site dated between 12-18th century CE.
data.legal_status: Protected by The Sindh Cultural Heritage (Preservation) Act 1994
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: Dheeru-jo-Daro is located approximately 2.76 km west of village Meeran Machi, it can be accessed from Meeran Machhi-Qamber road off earthen track to Dheeru-jo-Daro. Dheeru-jo-Daro is a large site, its measurements are 233 m in length, 144 m in breadth and about 1.8 m high from the surrounding cultivated area. The cultural material is sparsely scattered over the mound which comprises of plain and over fired pottery and one terracotta bead. The site is mostly damaged by natural agents and animal movements. There is a graveyard in the vicinity of the site.
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: The graveyard is known as Garhi Sher Muhammad Naich, it consists on one mosque known as Naich Khan Jamia Mosque, one tomb, one collapse structure and recent graves. Structure-01 (Naich Khan Jamia Mosque) Naich Khan Jamia mosque has a rectangular shaped courtyard with a boundary wall and wooden door on the east and south. The boundary/courtyard wall is surviving in a damaged condition. There are three marble graves in the courtyard. The mosque is rectangular in shape with facade on the eastern side, it is decorated with three recessed rectangular panels with recessed tudor arches and within these arches there are tudor arches with wooden doors and the recessed tudor arch panels blocked with wooden planks above the entrances. The spandrels of the central recessed tudor arches and all three wooden doors are further adorned with embossed floral motifs. On both sides of the central recessed rectangular panel, there are recessed tudor arches and rectangular panels. The western exterior wall has a mehrab and the southern and northern walls have two recessed tudor arches with wooden windows.
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: The site lies 735 m north-west of Badlo Khan Chandio village, it can be accessed from Maid Shahid village via earthen track to Karohar -Jo-Daro. It is a very large site, measuring approximately 45.7 m in length, 44.8 m in breadth and about 12 m. high from the surrounding cultivated area. There are evidences of a burnt brick wall, visible in the northern part of the mound exposed after illegal digging by the local people. Heavy concentration of cultural material was found on the site which clearly belonged to the Mature Indus period ranging between 2500-1850 B.C. The cultural material on the surface included: plain, painted, incised and perforated pottery of typical Mature Indus period, other material collected from surface comprised of potsherd with Indus script symbol, gray ware, terracotta bangles, lithic blades, stone ball, black stone and flakes. There is recent presence of graveyard on both (southern and eastern) sides of the site.
data.legal_status: Protected by The Sindh Cultural Heritage (Preservation) Act 1994
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: The archaeological site of Noazaman-jo- Daro is located about 6.33 Km North of Bhuthi Lashkar Khan, it can be accessed from Hamal Lake road. The archaeological site of Noazaman -Jo- Daro measures 106 m in length, 74 m in breadth and is 1.8 m high from surrounding level. The local people mentioned the site to have been once a very rich site, but its present condition does not portray any such evidence. The cultural material has been damaged due to presence of heavy salts on the site and during floods of 2010, presently the mound is occupied with recent graves. The cultural material on the surface comprised of plain, painted and black thin and thick pottery, it also included lids, handle, rim shards, body parts, three terracotta objects and sandstone.

data.description: Seehri Waro Daro is located about 1 Km north-east of village Qaim Khan Sheikh, it can be accessed via earthen track from village Qaim Khan Sheikh. The archaeological site of Seehri Waro Daro is a small mound. Its measurements are 36 m in length, 31.6 m in breadth and 1.8 m high from surroundings. The cultural material is sparsely spread on the site in a much-damaged condition due to the presence of salts in soil hence the site is yet unidentified (Islamic period?).
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.name_of_site: Tomb of Dado Aloodo Khan Guramani
data.description: The tomb of Aloodo Khan Guramani is located about 13 km north-west of Ghaibi Dero and about 1 km from Deenar Khan Buriro village. It can be accessed from Ghaibi Dero via Deenar Buriro village link road. The tomb of Aloodo Khan Guramani is located in Deenar Khan Buriro graveyard. The graveyard consists of one tomb structure and many recent graves in its vicinity. The architecture of the tomb resembles Kalhora Period architecture. The tomb is square in shape, it is constructed with burnt bricks, cheroli is used as mortar with lime plaster. Cement is used during repair work. The facade of the tomb is on the eastern side decorated with two multifoil arches and an iron door for the entrance. On either side of the multifoil arches, there are two recessed rectangular panels.

data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: Ghafoor Shah-Jo-Daro is located about 11.3 km northwest of Shahdadkot city. It can be accessed from Shahdadkot via Shahdadkot- Shaho Jamali village road turning southwest along the water channel to the site. There is a shrine of Ghafoor Shah located on the north-eastern edge of the mound and a graveyard on the eastern part of the mound. There are traces of burnt brick debris visible on the site perhaps there are structures beneath. The surface of the site had concentration of cultural material on the site. The cultural repertoire from the surface included plain red ware pottery thin & thick in texture with open and short rims, thin potshards with grooved lines on the outer surface, plain gray ware shards, one body part with a handle and a small hole, broken long necked water vessel, broken handle and knobs, terracotta wheel, shell pieces and a broken iron object. The site has been disturbed by the locals who have illegally dug in various parts of the mound.

data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: The graveyard of Aitbar Khan Chandio is located about 04 km east of Shahdadkot city and close to M-8 Motorway. It can be accessed from Rato Dero via Shahdadkot-Gwadar M-8 Motorway towards Shahdadkot city. The graveyard is known as Aitbar Khan Chandio graveyard. It consists of two tomb structures, one belonging to Rais Aitbar Khan Husnani Chandio and the other of Muhammad Khan Husnani Chandio with some old and recent structures and graves in the surrounding. The tomb I, belongs to Rais Aitbar Khan Husnani Chandio. The tomb structure is square in shape, it is constructed with burnt bricks with mud mortar and lime plaster. The facade of the tomb is on the eastern side, it is decorated with prominent outline border, the center of the facade has three recessed rectangular panels with the middle panel having multifoil arch decoration and a recessed rectangular panel, the lower panel has an arched entrance.

data.description: The graveyard of Darya Khan Mastoi is located about 04 km east of Shahdadkot city and close to M-8 motorway. It can be accessed from Rato Dero via Shahdadkot-Gwadar M-8 motorway towards to Shahdadkot city. The graveyard is known as Darya Khan Mastoi graveyard, who was a chief of Mastoi tribe. The graveyard consists of one tomb of Darya Khan Mastoi, one recent mosque and some old and recent graves. The tomb of Darya Khan Mastoi is square in shape and it is constructed with burnt bricks, mud is used as mortar with lime plaster.The facade of the tomb is on the eastern side, it is decorated with a prominent outline border. The central part of the facade has three recessed rectangular panels, the lower panel has a Tudor arch entrance and the middle panel has recessed Tudor arch panel. On either side of the middle part, there are two recessed Tudor arch panels with rectangular panels. The parapet wall is decorated with four closed kiosks on the corners and two in the center. Parapet wall is further decorated with merlons. The dome rests on the high octagonal drum. Around the drum there are recessed rectangular panels and the perimeter is adorned with merlons and small turrets. The top of the dome has inverted lotus flower mouldings with an iron rod as a finial

data.description: The graveyard of Haji Khan Khuhawar is in Shahdadkot city in Kamboh Mohalla. The tomb lies in Haji Khan Khuhawar graveyard. It consists of one Barrel vault tomb of Haji Khan Khuhawar and few recent structures and graves in the surroundings. The barrel vaulted roof tomb of Haji Khan Khuhawar is rectangular in plan, It is constructed with burnt bricks with mud (structure) and cheroli (only in aches) mortar and traditional lime plaster.The structure is divided into two parts; the front and the rear part. Both were barrel roofed but the roof of the rear part has collapsed. Both the structures adjoin each other and are connected with entrance from the rear wall of the first part of the structure. The facade of the structure is on the southern side, it is adorned with five recessed rectangular panels the central panel having recessed multifoil arch with a door, two side panels with multifoil arch and two corner having ogee arches. The Western side wall is decorated with three panels of recessed ogee arch with three recessed rectangular panels above.
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh

data.description: The Shinkhani Chandio graveyard is located about 13 km south-west of Ghaibi Dero and about 01 km from Deenar Khan Buriro village. It can be accessed from Ghaibi Dero via Deenar Buriro village link road. Shinkhani Chandio graveyard consists of one tomb known as Allahyar tomb and many old and recent graves in the surroundings. The tomb locally known as Allahyar jo Qubo is situated in Shinkhani Chandio graveyard. It is rectangular in shape and is constructed with burnt bricks with mud mortar and is without plaster. All four sides of the tomb are identical having an arched entrance in the center within recessed rectangular frame with recessed rectangular and arched panels on either side of the entrance. There is a row of recessed corbel arch panels above them. The tomb has vaulted-dome which has partially collapsed. Interior of the tomb has four squinches and the grave is decrepit in condition.

data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: The graveyard of Haji Khan Marri is located about 32 km north-west of Ghaibi Dero on a hillock. It can be accessed from Mazarani Gas Field towards Ali Jan Chandio village via jeep able track. Haji Khan Marri is buried in the graveyard named after him; he died during the battle of Gerallo. His tomb is believed to have been built by Mian Noor Muhammad Kalhoro. The tomb structure is enclosed within a low boundary wall with gateway facing east which has partially collapsed. There are two graves laid on the southern side of the tomb. The gateway has four arch openings on all sides, with a dome on top. The tomb structure is square in shape; it is constructed with burnt bricks with mud mortar and lime plaster. The facade of the tomb is on the eastern side, having recessed rectangular panel with large and small Tudor arches with an iron door for entrance.
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: Hairo Khan Thul is located about 24 km north-west of Johi town and about 01 km west of village Hairo Khan, it can be accessed from Johi via Hairo Khan link road towards Hairo Khan Thul. The Hairo Khan Thul/Stupa is located in village Hairo Khan in Taluka Johi District Dadu. The Thul is rectangular in shape. It is 73.9 m high from the ground level. Its width is 70.1 m at the base and it is narrow at the top. The Thul is built with mud bricks and baked bricks, cheroli and mud mortar is used as a binding material and cheroli is also used as a plaster in interior tunnel arch. On the southern and northern side of the Thul (at ground level), there are arched/curved openings/tunnels on both sides. The height of the arch is 1.5 m and width are 1 m. A stairway leads to the top of the stupa on the northern side. On the top of the stupa, there is evidence of a round shaped structure built with wedge shaped burnt bricks (Buddhist period).

data.description: The graveyard is situated at about 04 km north-east of Ghaibi Dero village, it can be accessed from Ghaibi Dero via earthen track towards Malik Ghaibi Khan Husnani Chandio Graveyard (Rankoon). The necropolis of Malik Ghaibi Khan Husnani Chandio (hereafter Ghaibi Khan Chandio graveyard) belongs to Kalhora period to the recent times. Ghaibi Khan was a leader and follower of the Mianwal movement of the 17th century CE and a descendant of Mirzani Chandias. The Necropolis consists of twenty-four (24) structures mostly tombs, some have completely collapsed.

data.description: Graveyard of Mast Qehar Shah is located in Rajo Dero village at a distance of about 7.63km north-west of Qasbo village, it can be accessed from Qasbo via link road towards Mast Qehar Shah graveyard and village. The graveyard of Mast Qehar Shah is also known as Lashkar Khan Leghari Graveyard. It consists of two canopies and Dargah of Mast Qehar Shah with seven other graves within the enclosure (recent). There are some old and recent graves in the surroundings. The architecture of the canopies resembles with Kalhora Period architecture. Of the two canopies one belongs to Baloch Khan and his son and the other belongs to Lashkar Khan Leghari and his wife. Baloch Khan and Lashkar Khan are known to be followers of the Mianwal Movement of the 17th century CE (Kalhora Period).

data.description: Shahdad Khan Khoso graveyard is located in village Chinni, about 20 km south-west of Johi city. It can be accessed from Johi via village Chinni link road towards Shahdad Khan Khoso graveyard. Shahdad Khan Khoso graveyard is also known as Chinni graveyard. It consists of 04 structures, (one tomb of Shahdad Khan Khoso and three unknown canopy structures) and many other old and recent graves within the graveyard. Historic documents mention Shahdad Khan Khoso being caretaker/controller of Chinni in the period of Mian Yaar Mohammad Kalhoro.

data.description: The Muglia site lies about 30 km north of Shah Godero Shrine. It can be accessed from Fareedabad via Shah Godero Shrine and onwards via Jeep able track crossing Mehar Gas Field to Mangli village. Mugli site lies on the eastern edge of the Khirthar hills, it is divided into two parts (Mound I & Mound II) by a rivulet flowing through it, the cultural material is profusely scattered on both sides of the rivulet on the mounds. There is evidence of stone fortification wall on the site of Mugli along with stone structures in the shape of small chambers, corridor and rooms besides some recent graves of Chandia tribe. The cultural material comprises of stone blades and pottery of Kot Dijian, Amrian and Nal periods. The site lies chronologically between 4th and 3rd millennium B.C. and is of great significance having evidence of the early Indus tradition, the formative stages of the Mature Indus period of the Indus civilization.
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: The tomb is located in village Dodai about 04 km north-east of Larkana, on Larkana-Naudero road to village Dodai. Pir Nasirudin Shah belonged to Syed family. His tomb was constructed by Chand Ram his devotee. The mausoleum consists of the one tomb, one mosque and one Haveli of British period. One recently constructed structure of the grave of the mother of Pir Nasirudin Shah and few graves are present near the tomb. The tomb is square in plan and is renovated with cement, Kashi tiles are re-fixed and the tomb has been white washed. The facade of the is on the eastern side and it is decorated with large deep recessed multifoil arch in the center with a carved wooden door within it and three recessed rectangular panels above it. On either sides of the central multifoil arch are eight recessed rectangular panels. There is a cornice around the tomb and six kiosks, two on the facade and four on the corners of the parapet wall. The facade is decorated with Kashi tiles and the parapet is adorned with Kashi musalas.
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: Labaran-Jo-Daro is located about 5.13 km north-west of Garhi Khuda Baksh near Noor Muhammad Buledi village. It can be accessed from Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto Mazar via earthen track to the site. Labaran-Jo-Daro is a large site measuring 725 m north-south and 332 m east-west, it is about 8 m high from the surrounding plains. The total area of the site is about 240700 sq. m. There is a village Sajan Labano consisting of nearly 40 houses on the southern part of the mound and a brick kiln on the eastern edge. The ceramics collected from the surface of the site comprised of plain, painted, few black colored and cloth impressed pottery. No diagnostic sherd was found hence period is unidentified (Islamic period?).
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: Rumi graveyard is located about 05 km west of Wahi Pandhi town, it can be accessed from Wahi Pandhi via Gorakh Hill Resort road cutting near stone crushing plant via earthen track towards Rumi graveyard on high hills of Khirthar mountains. The Rumi graves are found in various parts of Sindh and Baluchistan province, they are built in different shapes, style, design and decoration. Some are on high platform and some on low; these are known with different names viz. stone carved graves, Gharyoon and Rumi`s. Some believe that this style of graves originated before the arrival of the Persians in Sindh. One finds several platform-types of stone graves in Sindh especially in Karachi, Jamshoro and Dadu districts. There are two groups of Rumi graves on the bank of Nain Nali/Narri, near Wahi Pandhi. The first group of Rumi graves is located on the southern bank of Nain Nali and another cluster of Rumi graves lies on the northern bank of Nain Nali. Both groups of Rumi graves are at a distance of approx. 1.5 km from each other (Talpur period).
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: Tomb of Dayo Faqir is located about 2.4 km west of Khudabad mosque on N-55 (old Indus Highway) and can be accessed from N-55 via link road to Dayo Faqir tomb near Mian Yar Muhammad Kalhoro tomb complex. The tomb of Dayo Faqir is known to have been built during the reign of Mian Yar Mohammad Kalhoro (1701-1718). He was believed to have been a Wazir of Mian Yar Mohammad, perhaps deputed to deal with livestock affairs. The tomb of Dayo Faqir is oblong in plan, it is constructed with slop molded bricks, mud is used as mortar with lime plaster. The tomb has one opening which is on the eastern side. It is a vaulted-roof structure with walls provided with slanting eave and three recessed panels and arch openings of equal size on the east and the west and one recessed panel and arch opening on the northern and southern sides. The arch openings on the eastern, northern and western sides were provided with decorative perforated brick work (jali) but at present with the exception of one arch opening on the western side the rest have now lost this element. The spandrels of central arches on the east and the west are adorned with peacock motifs. The recessed panels above the arch openings on all the four sides of the tomb depict fruit dish patterns in fresco. The interior of the tomb is decorated with floral patterns. A single grave exists inside the tomb (Kalhora Period).
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: The Mankan Waro Daro is located approximately 02 km south-east of Fulji Station, it can be accessed from Fulji Station via link road to Qazi Pir Muhammad solangi Village and earthen track to Mankan Waro Daro. Mankan Waro Daro is also known as Manktaro and Manak Daro (hereafter Mankan Waro Daro). The local version is that, this area was ruled by Jam Jakhro, a Samma ruler. It is also mentioned by historians as an ancient Soomra period site. The site of Mankan Waro Daro is a very large site, the mound measures 362 m in length, 192 m in breadth and about 6 m high from the surrounding cultivated area. The cultural material on surface bears no such indication but can only be verified through archaeological intensive investigation of the site as burnt bricks and brick bats are found on the surface and mud bricks wall is evident in a section of a robber`s trench on the mound. The cultural material is scattered over the mound which perhaps belongs to the Islamic period, it includes: plain and painted pottery, incised design pottery and terracotta animal figurine. The southern part of the site has presence of recent graves. There was evidence of a mud brick wall noticed on the northern side of the high mound, where a robber`s trench was dug by local people. The major portion of the mound has been destroyed.
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: Khudabad mosque is located in Khudabad village on Indus highway (N-55), about 11 km south of Dadu city. The mosque is located in village Khudabad. It was built by Mian Yaar Muhammad Kalhoro during his reign and dates back to 1701-1718 CE It is enclosed within a compound wall, the main entrance to the mosque is through a gatehouse which faces east. The facade of the gatehouse is decorated with an arched alcove in the center with a large tudor arch within rectangular frame and wooden door for entrance. On either side of the tudor arch there are recessed rectangular panels, the interior top of the alcove is decorated with recessed tudor arch panel and two small squinches. The sides of the alcove are adorned with recessed rectangular panels. The facade is decorated with kashi tiles. The approach to the mosque is though semicircular steps of marble. The main mosque is rectangular in plan; its facade is on the eastern side, with three entrances. All these entrances are within arched alcoves, the central alcove is further adorned with recessed tudor arch. The interior of the alcoves has small squinches in the corners and recessed tudor arch panel in the center and honey-comb design above. The entrances within the alcoves are flanked by recessed tudor arches and rectangular frames. The right and the left sides of the smaller alcoves are adorned with two recessed tudor arch panel and two recessed rectangular panels.
data.legal_status: Protected by The Sindh Cultural Heritage (Preservation) Act 1994
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: Dada Budhal Shah complex is located in Borirri village about 10 km south-east of Khairpur Nathan Shah, it can be accessed from National Highway N-55 Kakkar towards Borirri village. The Dada Budhal Shah tomb and mosque are located in Borirri village, the tomb and mosque architecture resembles with Kalhora and Talpur period architecture. There are no historic records so far traceable. The tomb is enclosed within a compound wall (recent) with wooden door on the northern side. Other structures within this compound wall are some old and recent graves and one funerary structure (recent) belonging to Syed family. The tomb is rectangular in shape on its exterior side and almost square in its interior, it is constructed with burnt bricks, mud is used as mortar with lime plaster and repaired with cement.

data.description: Maroo Thul is located about 6 km north-east of Faridabad, it can be accessed from Mehar via Fareedabad link road toward Qadir Bux Rind Village near Maroo thul.The exterior or outer part of Maroo Thul is irregular in shape, its northern side length is 14.3 m and eastern side width is 1.5 m and western side width 3 m. It is constructed with mud bricks with mud mortar. There are traces of stairs leading to the top of the Thul on the western side. The inner core of the Thul is cylindrical in shape, its diameter is 1.2 m (inner side) and 2.4-2.4 m (outer part), the width of brick masonry is 0.6-0.9 m, the height of the outer wall and the inner core is 3.6 m. It is constructed with burnt bricks and mud mortar. The inner core and the external mud structure have partially collapsed.

data.description: This tomb is located in Mian Noor Muhammad Kalhora graveyard, Nawab Shah. It is square in plan and measures 7.70x7.70x16m. It is made up of burnt bricks, mud mortar, lime mortar and glazed tiles. A pointed arch door having multi-cusp edges within a large deep multi-cusp arched frame is provided at the entrance. Low dome has been erected on octagonal drum crowned with thick finial or lantern. Interior chamber is decorated with deep recessed arch panels in each wall with multi-cusp panels. The tomb is associated to Kalhora period of Historic Sindh (1700-1783 CE).
data.title: Nawab Shah: The Lost Glory

data.description: Tomb is situated in old Muhammad village. Masu Wah flowing west side of tomb, Sui Sharif village is about 1 km south of tomb, while Ubaro taluka is 12 km in east of tomb. Hall of tomb ha a flat roof, four ventilators on north and four on south while three each on east and west. Twenty seven graves of family members are found inside the tomb. There is no decoration on the tomb. It is probably associated to Kalhora period of Sindh.

data.description: Bird`s place is located in deh, taluka, district Jacobabad. It is in north of Deputy Commissioner`s residence and in east of S.D. M`s office. There are four arch shape doors, one in each side. The first phase has a room, second phase have seven rows, each row contains 36 rectangular holes for pigeon`s nests. This building has 252 nests for pigeons. These nests are in wall and this building has no roof in the center. There are four cemented pillars with thin beams of wood on the top. Burnt bricks and mud mortar are construction materials. It is square in plan. It exists in good condition. It was renovated in 1990-91 by government.

data.description: The site of Bukhar Daro lies approximately 8.8 km north-east of Badin city. It can be accessed from Badin-Bypass Road towards Canal Road connecting earthen track to Mubarak Mallah village. The site of Bukhari Daro is a large mound measuring 266 m in length, 255 m in breadth, it is about 7.6 m high from the surrounding surface. The site is ruined in condition and at a high risk. It is encroached by recent graves on its south-western side. The site is possibly related to Sultanate/Mughal period.
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh

data.description: Veer Thari site is located about 7 km south-east of Seerani town. It can be accessed from Bhugra Memon link road via earthen track to Veer Thari site.  Thari is a large site divided into two parts, Mound-I (Southern) and Mound-II (Northern). Mound I and II are at a distance of about 11.65 m. Mound-I measures 75 m in length, 21.3 m in breadth, it is about 2.7 m high from the surrounding plain. The measurements of mound-II are 107 m in length, 17.4 m in breadth and about 2.7 m high from the surrounding plains. The cultural material was profusely scattered over the site, which probably belonged to the Buddhist period (3rd-8th Century CE).
data.title: Documentation of the Heritage Sites and Monuments of Sindh
data.published_in: Endowment Fund Trust for Preservation of the Heritage of Sindh
